Concept: Roles of different RNA types in Protein Synthesis

Solution:

All three major classes of RNA are necessary for protein synthesis (translation):

  • mRNA (messenger RNA): Serves as the template or blueprint carrying the genetic code from DNA.

  • tRNA (transfer RNA): Functions as the adapter molecule, carrying specific amino acids to the ribosome and matching them to the mRNA codons.

  • rRNA (ribosomal RNA): Is the structural and catalytic component of the ribosome, providing the framework and possessing the peptidyl transferase activity.

    hnRNA (heterogeneous nuclear RNA) is the precursor to mRNA in eukaryotes, but it is not directly involved in translation itself.

    Final Answer: 1
